existing_certifications.g11_qualification: Mandatory RTL A/B is separately blocked by absent candidate artifact and certified vLLM toolchain; no replacement was promoted.

audit_items.finding: Logical-subagent JSON results over 128000 UTF-8 bytes raise subagent_result_too_large; _execute maps LogicalSubagentError to FAILED.
A non-available or insufficient GPU observation immediately completes a task as GPU_BLOCKED and the dispatcher does not requeue or wait for capacity.
REAL_CONCURRENT admission is limited by active count and a shared GPU observation; there is no race-safe aggregate VRAM reservation ledger.
Completed outcomes are retained in an unbounded in-process _completed dictionary; no retention bound or durable externalization is present in this scheduler.
run_batch establishes one common deadline before waiting entries, so queue delay consumed by earlier tasks reduces later task wall budget.
Bounded ACI rejects reads beyond 400 lines or 32000 output characters and performs one-shot bounded edits/files without continuation cursors or chunk transactions.
SQLite memory initialization overwrites an existing schema marker with the current version, including a newer unsupported version, rather than negotiating or failing closed.
C/C++ and Verilog/SystemVerilog repository intelligence uses line-oriented regular expressions; multiline C declarations and parameterized RTL constructs are not parsed as production grammar.
Hook timeout cancels the Future and returns hook_timeout, but an already-running Python callback remains executable in its worker thread.
LaplaceCore imports and constructs ZetsuAgentCoordinator and directly calls its private _verify_argv implementation.

The prior G11 certification records the mandatory CodeV-vs-SiliconMind RTL A/B as blocked by absent candidate artifact/config/tensors and missing certified vLLM toolchain; no replacement result was promoted.
Package metadata remains version 0.7.0 and the README still presents the v0.7/Ollama-era product description rather than the actual v2 system.
